answer:
Use **Hyperframes as the sole picture renderer and timeline owner**, adapting the existing-artwork montage route from [router/SKILL.md](router/SKILL.md). The supplied registry reports tested image pan/zoom, transitions, timelines and video export in Hyperframes 0.8.157. That matches these inputs; the watercolor appearance comes from the approved paintings. **This exact seamless-loop integration remains untested.**

The plan uses the three illustrations as flat image layers, labelled A, B and C until their identities are available. Preserve their brushwork, palette and texture. Add only restrained translation, scaling and opacity transitions. No repainting, generated imagery, depth reconstruction, narration, music or sound effects. No added text is proposed: compared with `product.md`, the plan introduces no product claims or CTA.

Canvas dimensions remain provisional until the artwork dimensions and intended display are known. Prefer a canvas that preserves the approved compositions; avoid stretching or unapproved cropping. Use a proposed 30 fps timeline: **300 frames, exactly 10 seconds**, with end-exclusive frame ranges.

| Frames / time | Picture and motion |
|---|---|
| 0–75 / 0–2.5 s | A, with a very slow, small pan or scale change. |
| 75–105 / 2.5–3.5 s | Smooth one-second dissolve from A to B. |
| 105–180 / 3.5–6 s | B, continuing restrained motion. |
| 180–210 / 6–7 s | Smooth one-second dissolve from B to C. |
| 210–270 / 7–9 s | C, with similarly restrained motion. |
| 270–300 / 9–10 s | Dissolve from C back to A, reaching A’s opening composition at the conceptual 10-second endpoint. |

These are master-timeline intervals, so transitions are already included in the ten seconds.

For the **end-to-start seam**, define every transform and opacity from seekable timeline time. Give A a periodic motion curve whose position, scale and velocity agree at 0 and 10 seconds. Use eased opacity transitions with zero slope at their endpoints. Continue the same A layer through the wrap; do not restart its movement on reappearance. Encode frames 0–299 without appending a duplicate endpoint frame, which could create a pause. The last encoded frame should advance naturally into frame 0; pixel identity between those adjacent samples is not required.

Before future production, confirm the three approved asset identities, dimensions, colour profiles, permitted use and crop constraints. Approval is stated in the request; the actual files have not been inspected. Runtime preflight is **blocked** by absent guides and runtimes: read the installed Hyperframes instructions, verify its API, pin a compatible version, and check runtime and asset licence terms. Nothing has been installed or rendered.

The intended production artifact is a silent `watercolor-loop.mp4`, provisionally H.264 with a flattened background, accompanied by the composition settings and an honest QA record. No thumbnail, captions or separate audio output is requested.

A bounded future integration trial would render only this proposed 300-frame loop. Pass conditions are: decoded duration and frame count match the plan; artwork retains acceptable colour, detail and framing; dissolves show no distracting ghosting or flicker; and repeated playback shows no jump, flash, freeze or motion reset at any transition, especially frame 299→0. Inspect that boundary frame by frame and watch at least three repetitions. Confirm absence of audio, record output settings and hash, and obtain visual acceptance separately. answer:
**No—the present paid subscription alone does not establish commercial clearance for the old song or its existing song-card video.** For this comparison, the proposed product ad remains uncleared on the supplied evidence.

| Element | What your evidence establishes | What remains unresolved |
|---|---|---|
| Your lyrics | You own the supplied words. | That ownership does not itself license Suno’s generated recording or visuals. |
| Song generated on Free | Its creation predates your paid subscription. | Current paid status does not establish a retroactive commercial grant for that song. |
| Existing song-card video | It is a native song-card asset you want to reuse. | Export availability does not establish commercial permission for its audio, artwork or other visual components. |
| Current paid account | You now have paid access. | Plan access and rights attached to an older asset are separate questions. |

The router’s Suno profile specifically warns against inferring commercial clearance from a playable library item or current paid status alone. Its music guidance also separates technical export availability from permitted use. A commercial product ad requires permission covering that intended use.

Evidence that could change this conclusion would be applicable terms explicitly covering retroactive use, or an asset-specific grant covering the old recording and the card’s visual components. Neither is supplied. Owning the lyrics resolves one input-rights question, but does not fill those gaps.

This is an evidence-based clearance comparison, not a determination that permission could never be obtained. I used the supplied local guidance; I have not checked live terms, account history or the actual media. No generation or account actions were taken.
